result.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed.import_remote whitelists `attributes: %w[href src]`, preserving hrefs while the raw-HTML cook path (cook_method :raw_html renders raw unmodified) means a `javascript:` href from the retrieved remote page would pass through untouched into `post.cooked` and be rendered via `raw post.cooked` in the embed view. The URL scheme check in import only validates the embed URL, not link contents, so the mechanism described is real.

judged_text: import_remote's readability whitelist (tags/attributes) strips on* handlers but still passes javascript: hrefs

record.issue_text: import_remote's readability whitelist (tags/attributes) strips on* handlers but still passes javascript: hrefs

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` builds `Readability::Document` with `attributes: %w[href src]` and then imports `doc.content` into a post created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which causes `Post#cook` to return `raw` and bypass the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Given that `href` is explicitly allowed and there is no additional filtering in the diff to restrict URL schemes, malicious `javascript:` links (or similar) in the remote HTML could be persisted and rendered as-is, creating an XSS vector. The diff does not show any scheme validation or sanitization of `href`/`src` beyond the attribute whitelist.
